claims.note: Rerun: 'python checks/check_C00126.py measure' (the assertion stage; prep/tokenizer/fit/clean/sft are earlier stages whose outputs already exist) in image p9pilot-srgpmdqjjm reproduced the recorded output exactly (S1-S4 PASS; CR 0.2118, E∩D=0, 200/200 new rows changed, 0.4975 percent, BPC 1.3628 -> 0.7299, cosine 0.9975 -> 0.9737); the regenerated C00126_summary.json was byte-identical to the original (original restored, copy saved as work/logs/C00126_summary.confirm.json). Stronger replication on a scratch copy outside the workspace (checks/repo/data copied, tpe_tokenizers, tpe_models, cleaned_SFT_QA and the SSFT checkpoint deleted, then tokenizer -> fit -> clean -> checks/ssft_minimal.py -> measure): all four stages pass again, with S1/S2 identical in verdict and S3 fraction 0.4975 percent, but the numbers move: the repo tokenizer step is not bit-reproducible (MedTPE token count 99538 vs 99543, so some of the 200 pairs differ run to run), ssft_minimal reached 135 vs 117 updates under its wall-clock cap, BPC after SSFT 0.6947 (CI of the change [-0.691,-0.644]) vs 0.7299, cosine after 0.9620 vs 0.9737 (CI below 0 again). Side note: with fit stages re-run but the old SSFT checkpoint kept, S3/S4 still print PASS although the checkpoint no longer matches the re-fitted pairs, so those two numbers are only meaningful when the checkpoint and the TPE model come from the same run. Does the check test the claim as worded: yes for the descriptive mechanism (lossless 2-token merges, size-preserving dependency-aware eviction that spares sub-tokens and their merge paths, only new-token rows trained), using the repo's own scripts and an independently recomputed dependency set; but with limits that the 'consistent' label should carry: (1) 'least-common' is only weakly tested because all 200 evicted tokens and the rarest retained eligible token have frequency 0 (ties), so any zero-frequency choice would pass; (2) the roughly 3 percent is an input (M=200 of 6000 chosen by the experimenter; 5000/151936 from the paper), not an observed repo behaviour; (3) SSFT in S3/S4 is a minimal fp32 AdamW loop (lr 5e-4, about 120-135 updates, 1.06M-param stand-in LM) around the repo's embedding-split module, not llm_sft.py, so the shipped bf16/Adam8bit trainer was never exercised; (4) the 0.5-1.0 percent range is arithmetic on the public Qwen2.5-1.5B config (0.4975 percent) that passes only through the pre-registered rounding to 0.1 pp, and the untied Qwen2.5-7B gives 0.235 or 0.471 percent, below the range, excluded from the pass rule; (5) 'aligns with the pretrained latent space' is operationalised by held-out BPC of the model's own pseudo-labels, which is close to the SFT training objective (57-60 percent of the gap to the original model closed, never reaching it), while the more direct hidden-state cosine to the original model decreases after SSFT in both runs, so alignment is supported only in the loss sense. These are power or construct-validity qualifications, none contradicts the recorded 'consistent' under the pre-registered rule.
